To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

TCF7L is a master regulator in the pancreatic β-cell that controls insulin synthesis and secretion by regulation of a network of transcription factors and genes involved in insulin synthesis, processing and secretion.
we identified a TCF-7L2-regulatory transcriptional network that controls insulin production and processing via ISL1, MAFA, PDK-1, NKX-6.1, PC-1/2, SLC-30A8 and other transcriptional targets.
we identified a TCF-7L2-regulatetranscriptional network responsible for T2D risk.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel molecular mechanisms of insulin secretion, and the elucidation of genetic variants in TCF/L2 and other genes that affect these mechanisms.

a better understanding of the molecular mechanisms by which the genetic risk variants of T2D act on pancreatic islet cells, and the functional consequences of these variants on the regulation of insulin production, processing and secretion.

the identification of the molecular pathways that link TCF7L 2 to T2D, which will provide novel insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying T2D and may lead to the development of novel therapies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TCF7L is a master regulator for the transcription of a network of genes that regulate insulin synthesis and processing, which is important for normal glucose homeostasis.
TCF7L is a master regulator in insulin production and processing in pancreatic islets.
TCF7L1 is a master regulator in the insulin production and processing, which is important for the understanding of the pathophysiological mechanism of T2D.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified a novel TCF7L 2-ISL1 regulatory network that controls proinsulin production, processing and secretion, and this network is dysregulated in individuals carrying the high-risk T-allele
TCF7L1/2 are key regulators of insulin production and secretion in pancreatic beta cells and that TCF7l2 is a major regulator of insulin production in humans.
TCF7L1 and TCF7L4, the closest homologs of TCF7l2, have similar functions and the T-allele of TCF7 is a risk factor for type 2 diabetes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transcription factor TCF7L is a central regulator of insulin production, processing and possibly secretion in the pancreatic β cell.
TCF7L1/2 is a master transcriptional regulator of insulin production, processing, and secretion, and that the T2D-associated variants in TCF1/7L2 affect these processes in pancreatic islets.
the risk T-allele is associated with increased Tcf7l2 expression and reduced insulin content in human islets.
